messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Data simulation for negative binomial Nmix model
parts:
Dear unmarkers,

I am trying to simulate data under an N-mixture model with a negative binomial mixture for latent abundance N using R function rnbinom(n, size, prob, mu). Part of what the R help file says is this:

"An alternative parametrization (often used in ecology) is by the mean mu, and size, the dispersion parameter, where prob = size/(size+mu)."

So, I simulate the latent N's as this, where beta0=1, beta1=-1 and dispersion = 10 in my first trial:

x1 <- seq(-2, 2,, M)       # Site covariate

lambda <- exp(beta0 + beta1 * x1)

size <- dispersion      # Dispersion parameter

N <- rnbinom(n = length(x), mu = lambda, size = dispersion)


(I also have a detection model with one observational covariate, but that's of no importance here.)

When I simulate 100 data sets and analyse them in unmarked using pcount with the data-generating model, I get what look like unbiased estimates for the regression parameters (red is the truth, blue the mean of 100 estimates), but the estimates of the "dispersion parameter" are way off; see attached figure.

Does anybody know how the dispersion parameter in unmarked is defined ?

Thanks and kind regards  --  Marc

btw, if anybody's interested, here is the function, regards  ---  Marc

# Simulate Nmix data with NegBin abundance distribution

NB.data <- function(M = 267, T = 3, alpha0 = 1, alpha1 = -1, beta0 = -1, beta1 = 1, dispersion = 10){

 

# Function simulates data for the Nmix model with
# a negative binomial abundance distribution.

# alpha0 and alpha1 are the intercept and the slope of a logistic-linear
# regression of detection probability on an observation covariate x2.

# beta0 and beta1 are the intercept and the slope of a log-linear
# regression of expected abundance on a site covariate x1.

# M is the number of sites and T the number of temporal reps.

# dispersion is the negative binomial dispersion parameter, with
# lower values corresponding to increasing aggregation.

 

# Abundance model

x1 <- seq(-2, 2,, M)       # Site covariate

lambda <- exp(beta0 + beta1 * x1)

size <- dispersion      # Dispersion parameter

N <- rnbinom(n = length(x), mu = lambda, size = dispersion)

par(mfrow = c(2,2))

plot(x1, lambda, main = "Relationship x1-lambda")

hist(N, main = "Histogram of latent N", breaks = 50, col = "grey")

 

# Detection model

x2 <- matrix(rnorm(M*T), ncol = T)    # Observational covariate

p <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * x2)

plot(x2, p, main = "Relationship x2-p")

C <- array(dim = c(M,T))

for(j in 1:T){

   C[,j] <- rbinom(M, N, p[,j])

}

hist(C, main = "Histogram of counts C", breaks = 50, col = "grey")

# Output

return(list(M=M, T=T, alpha0=alpha0, alpha1=alpha1, beta0=beta0, beta1=beta1, dispersion=dispersion, x1=x1, x2=x2, lambda=lambda, N=N, p=p, C=C))

}

 

# Check how it works

NB.data()

NB.data(alpha1=0, beta1=0)

NB.data(alpha1=-2, beta1=2)

NB.data(alpha1=-2, beta1=2, dispersion = 0.1)

NB.data(alpha0=0, alpha1=1, beta0 = 1, beta1=-1, dispersion = 10)
